knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Dot Product Using the General Formula

question.:question/worked-solution:
The dot product of two vectors given in component form can be computed by summing up the products of corresponding components of vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}q\cdot r & ={q}_{x}\cdot {r}_{x}+{q}_{y}\cdot {r}_{y}+{q}_{z}\cdot {r}_{z}\end{aligned}
$$

For these vectors, we have $q=⟨12,1,-11⟩$ and $r=⟨-4,4,3⟩.$ Therefore, the formula for the dot product gives

$$
\begin{aligned}q\cdot r & =12\cdot (-4)+1\cdot 4+(-11)\cdot 3 \\  & =-48+4-33 \\  & =-77.\end{aligned}
$$
